subtopics.title: The Two Original Participants — Households and Firms

questions.question: In the circular flow, what do households supply to firms through the factor market?
options: Goods and services
The factors of production — natural resources, labour, capital and entrepreneurship
Taxes and savings
Imported products

questions.question: Which factor income is paid for the use of capital?
options: Wages
Rent
Interest
Profit

questions.question: What is the difference between real flows and money flows?
options: Real flows are physical (factors, goods and services); money flows are the payments moving in the opposite direction
Real flows happen in real economies; money flows only in models
Real flows involve government; money flows involve banks
There is no difference — they are two names for the same arrows

subtopics.title: Leakages and Injections — Why the Circle Shrinks and Grows

questions.question: Why is saving classified as a leakage?
options: Because saved money is destroyed
Because it is income earned but not passed back to firms as spending
Because banks charge fees on savings
Because saving is bad for households

questions.question: How do savings re-enter the circular flow?
options: They cannot re-enter once withdrawn
Through taxes collected on bank accounts
Banks lend them to firms, which spend them on capital goods — investment
Households eventually spend them on imports

questions.question: If total leakages exceed total injections, the economy will:
options: Expand, because money is being stored safely
Contract — less money returns to firms each round, so production and incomes fall
Stay in equilibrium
Automatically increase exports

questions.question: A learner says 'leakages are bad and injections are good'. What is the correct view?
options: The learner is right — leakages should be banned
Leakage and injection describe the direction of flow, not virtue — savings, for example, finance future investment
Injections are actually bad because they cause inflation
Both terms only apply to government

subtopics.title: Adding Government — Taxes In, Spending Out

questions.question: Which pair correctly shows government's leakage and injection?
options: Leakage: government spending; injection: taxes
Leakage: taxes; injection: government spending
Leakage: imports; injection: exports
Leakage: savings; injection: investment

questions.question: On the circular flow diagram, why does government have arrows to BOTH households and firms?
options: It collects taxes from both and provides spending and public services to both
It only interacts with firms
It replaces the factor market
The arrows are decorative

questions.question: An economy with households, firms and government but no foreign trade is called:
options: An open economy
A market economy
A closed economy
A mixed economy

subtopics.title: The Foreign Sector — Opening the Economy

questions.question: Why are imports a leakage from South Africa's circular flow?
options: Because imported goods are lower quality
Because money earned inside the country is paid to firms outside the country
Because imports are taxed
Because imports increase production at home

questions.question: Which list gives the three leakages of the open economy?
options: Savings, taxes, imports
Investment, government spending, exports
Savings, exports, taxes
Wages, rent, interest

questions.question: A South African firm ships wine to Britain. In the circular flow this is:
options: A leakage, because the wine leaves the country
An injection, because foreign money flows into South African firms
Neither — foreign trade is outside the model
A leakage, because it reduces local wine supply

questions.question: Each leakage has a matching injection through the same channel. Which pairing is correct?
options: Savings and exports through the goods market
Taxes and investment through the financial sector
Imports and government spending through the factor market
Savings and investment through the financial sector
